author: buchanan_robert
text: The sun came up, and no one had died that night. The stars twinkled, but they were just like usual. In front of the house stood an old oak tree covered by snow, and around the branches hung some snowflakes. It seemed so peaceful and quiet outside; nothing happened at all! All of a sudden, I woke up from my dream—it was as if someone turned on the light.

author: buchanan_robert
text:
The day was gray as dawn on the mountain tops,

When I went out for a walk that last fall.

The wind blew hard through my bare arms and legs,

But still I walked along the road of yellow.

In his new book, The Best of Us, Bill Cosby discusses what it is that he would tell his children about being black and African-American today.  His advice: “Don’t listen to all this noise; don’t believe everything you hear on television or read in magazines.”

How does one encourage youth not to listen? How can one help them to trust their own sense of self over that which they are told by others? What kind of wisdom might be gleaned from an artist who knows how to make us laugh?

author: cushag
text: The children were happy and well-behaved when they had their mother with them. They played together happily until she called “Mayry.” Then all her attention was turned to one particular child, and he would run after it as long as possible. The other members of the family watched him do this, not being able to restrain themselves from laughter. So much did his mother think of her son that she forgot to give him food or drink, so he became tired and fell asleep during dinner. His father ran out into the yard to fetch some water, but the boy was already dead.

author: john_masefield
text:
"Down by the creek she walks with care,
But one day her mind grew strange;
She sat at home all alone,
With fear and dread that came.
To see those people go away from her,
Was not what it seemed.
So she cried out "Go back for me",
Till no sound could be heard.

A week went past when he returned,
Her eyes were full of tears,
For now his face is gone but she knows
That they are here still!

The Poem:

You are sitting there like an old man. You look out into space with eyes that have seen too much and remember more than you can put to words now. The memory of your life drifts away on a breeze like smoke from the mouth of some distant fire. There was once something very important to be done but now all you want is to go home, lay down and die.

I am writing this because I fear I will forget it.

author: stothert_james_a
text:
The sun was setting, and it was time for me to bid farewell.

I had walked many miles along this dusty road, seeking peace and quiet in my own way. But as I stood at the edge of town, watching the last rays of sunlight cast long shadows on the hills around us, an overwhelming sense of sadness washed over me.

My heart felt heavy with loss; not just because I would be leaving behind familiar faces but also because something deep inside knew that tomorrow morning would bring new challenges filled with uncertainty.
